scene.label: Act 1, Scene 3
scene.title: SCENE III. The same. A street.

content.text: Thunder and lightning. Enter, from opposite sides, Casca with his sword drawn, and Cicero.

lines.text: Good even, Casca: brought you Caesar home?
lines.plainText: Good even Casca brought you Caesar home

lines.text: Why are you breathless, and why stare you so?
lines.plainText: Why are you breathless and why stare you so

lines.text: Are not you moved, when all the sway of earth
lines.plainText: Are not you moved when all the sway of earth

lines.text: Shakes like a thing unfirm? O Cicero,
lines.plainText: Shakes like a thing unfirm O Cicero

lines.text: I have seen tempests, when the scolding winds
lines.plainText: I have seen tempests when the scolding winds

lines.text: Have riv'd the knotty oaks; and I have seen
lines.plainText: Have riv'd the knotty oaks and I have seen

lines.text: Th' ambitious ocean swell and rage and foam,
lines.plainText: Th' ambitious ocean swell and rage and foam

lines.text: To be exalted with the threatening clouds:
lines.plainText: To be exalted with the threatening clouds

lines.text: But never till tonight, never till now,
lines.plainText: But never till tonight never till now

lines.text: Did I go through a tempest dropping fire.
lines.plainText: Did I go through a tempest dropping fire

lines.text: Either there is a civil strife in heaven,
lines.plainText: Either there is a civil strife in heaven

lines.text: Or else the world too saucy with the gods,
lines.plainText: Or else the world too saucy with the gods

lines.text: Incenses them to send destruction.
lines.plainText: Incenses them to send destruction

lines.text: Why, saw you anything more wonderful?
lines.plainText: Why saw you anything more wonderful

lines.text: A common slave, you'd know him well by sight,
lines.plainText: A common slave you'd know him well by sight

lines.text: Held up his left hand, which did flame and burn
lines.plainText: Held up his left hand which did flame and burn

lines.text: Like twenty torches join'd, and yet his hand,
lines.plainText: Like twenty torches join'd and yet his hand

lines.text: Not sensible of fire remain'd unscorch'd.
lines.plainText: Not sensible of fire remain'd unscorch'd

lines.text: Besides, I ha' not since put up my sword,
lines.plainText: Besides I ha' not since put up my sword

lines.text: Against the Capitol I met a lion,
lines.plainText: Against the Capitol I met a lion

lines.text: Who glared upon me, and went surly by,
lines.plainText: Who glared upon me and went surly by

lines.text: Without annoying me. And there were drawn
lines.plainText: Without annoying me And there were drawn

lines.text: Upon a heap a hundred ghastly women,
lines.plainText: Upon a heap a hundred ghastly women

lines.text: Transformed with their fear; who swore they saw
lines.plainText: Transformed with their fear who swore they saw

lines.text: Men, all in fire, walk up and down the streets.
lines.plainText: Men all in fire walk up and down the streets

lines.text: And yesterday the bird of night did sit,
lines.plainText: And yesterday the bird of night did sit

lines.text: Even at noonday upon the marketplace,
lines.plainText: Even at noonday upon the marketplace

lines.text: Hooting and shrieking. When these prodigies
lines.plainText: Hooting and shrieking When these prodigies

lines.text: Do so conjointly meet, let not men say,
lines.plainText: Do so conjointly meet let not men say

lines.text: "These are their reasons; they are natural";
lines.plainText: These are their reasons they are natural

lines.text: For I believe, they are portentous things
lines.plainText: For I believe they are portentous things

lines.text: Unto the climate that they point upon.
lines.plainText: Unto the climate that they point upon

lines.text: Indeed, it is a strange-disposed time.
lines.plainText: Indeed it is a strangedisposed time

lines.text: But men may construe things after their fashion,
lines.plainText: But men may construe things after their fashion

lines.text: Clean from the purpose of the things themselves.
lines.plainText: Clean from the purpose of the things themselves

lines.text: Comes Caesar to the Capitol tomorrow?
lines.plainText: Comes Caesar to the Capitol tomorrow

lines.text: He doth, for he did bid Antonius
lines.plainText: He doth for he did bid Antonius

lines.text: Send word to you he would be there tomorrow.
lines.plainText: Send word to you he would be there tomorrow

lines.text: Goodnight then, Casca: this disturbed sky
lines.plainText: Goodnight then Casca this disturbed sky

lines.text: Is not to walk in.
lines.plainText: Is not to walk in

lines.text: Farewell, Cicero.
lines.plainText: Farewell Cicero

lines.text: Who's there?
lines.plainText: Who's there

lines.text: A Roman.
lines.plainText: A Roman

lines.text: Casca, by your voice.
lines.plainText: Casca by your voice

lines.text: Your ear is good. Cassius, what night is this!
lines.plainText: Your ear is good Cassius what night is this

lines.text: A very pleasing night to honest men.
lines.plainText: A very pleasing night to honest men

lines.text: Who ever knew the heavens menace so?
lines.plainText: Who ever knew the heavens menace so

lines.text: Those that have known the earth so full of faults.
lines.plainText: Those that have known the earth so full of faults

lines.text: For my part, I have walk'd about the streets,
lines.plainText: For my part I have walk'd about the streets

lines.text: Submitting me unto the perilous night;
lines.plainText: Submitting me unto the perilous night

lines.text: And, thus unbraced, Casca, as you see,
lines.plainText: And thus unbraced Casca as you see

lines.text: Have bar'd my bosom to the thunder-stone;
lines.plainText: Have bar'd my bosom to the thunderstone

lines.text: And when the cross blue lightning seem'd to open
lines.plainText: And when the cross blue lightning seem'd to open

lines.text: The breast of heaven, I did present myself
lines.plainText: The breast of heaven I did present myself

lines.text: Even in the aim and very flash of it.
lines.plainText: Even in the aim and very flash of it

lines.text: But wherefore did you so much tempt the Heavens?
lines.plainText: But wherefore did you so much tempt the Heavens

lines.text: It is the part of men to fear and tremble,
lines.plainText: It is the part of men to fear and tremble

lines.text: When the most mighty gods by tokens send
lines.plainText: When the most mighty gods by tokens send

lines.text: Such dreadful heralds to astonish us.
lines.plainText: Such dreadful heralds to astonish us

lines.text: You are dull, Casca; and those sparks of life
lines.plainText: You are dull Casca and those sparks of life

lines.text: That should be in a Roman you do want,
lines.plainText: That should be in a Roman you do want

lines.text: Or else you use not. You look pale and gaze,
lines.plainText: Or else you use not You look pale and gaze

lines.text: And put on fear and cast yourself in wonder,
lines.plainText: And put on fear and cast yourself in wonder

lines.text: To see the strange impatience of the Heavens:
lines.plainText: To see the strange impatience of the Heavens

lines.text: But if you would consider the true cause
lines.plainText: But if you would consider the true cause

lines.text: Why all these fires, why all these gliding ghosts,
lines.plainText: Why all these fires why all these gliding ghosts

lines.text: Why birds and beasts, from quality and kind;
lines.plainText: Why birds and beasts from quality and kind

lines.text: Why old men, fools, and children calculate,
lines.plainText: Why old men fools and children calculate

lines.text: Why all these things change from their ordinance,
lines.plainText: Why all these things change from their ordinance

lines.text: Their natures, and pre-formed faculties,
lines.plainText: Their natures and preformed faculties

lines.text: To monstrous quality; why, you shall find
lines.plainText: To monstrous quality why you shall find

lines.text: That Heaven hath infus'd them with these spirits,
lines.plainText: That Heaven hath infus'd them with these spirits

lines.text: To make them instruments of fear and warning
lines.plainText: To make them instruments of fear and warning

lines.text: Unto some monstrous state.
lines.plainText: Unto some monstrous state

lines.text: Now could I, Casca, name to thee a man
lines.plainText: Now could I Casca name to thee a man

lines.text: Most like this dreadful night,
lines.plainText: Most like this dreadful night

lines.text: That thunders, lightens, opens graves, and roars,
lines.plainText: That thunders lightens opens graves and roars

lines.text: As doth the lion in the Capitol;
lines.plainText: As doth the lion in the Capitol

lines.text: A man no mightier than thyself, or me,
lines.plainText: A man no mightier than thyself or me

lines.text: In personal action; yet prodigious grown,
lines.plainText: In personal action yet prodigious grown

lines.text: And fearful, as these strange eruptions are.
lines.plainText: And fearful as these strange eruptions are

lines.text: 'Tis Caesar that you mean; is it not, Cassius?
lines.plainText: 'Tis Caesar that you mean is it not Cassius

lines.text: Let it be who it is: for Romans now
lines.plainText: Let it be who it is for Romans now

lines.text: Have thews and limbs like to their ancestors;
lines.plainText: Have thews and limbs like to their ancestors

lines.text: But, woe the while! our fathers' minds are dead,
lines.plainText: But woe the while our fathers' minds are dead

lines.text: And we are govern'd with our mothers' spirits;
lines.plainText: And we are govern'd with our mothers' spirits

lines.text: Our yoke and sufferance show us womanish.
lines.plainText: Our yoke and sufferance show us womanish

lines.text: Indeed, they say the senators tomorrow
lines.plainText: Indeed they say the senators tomorrow

lines.text: Mean to establish Caesar as a king;
lines.plainText: Mean to establish Caesar as a king

lines.text: And he shall wear his crown by sea and land,
lines.plainText: And he shall wear his crown by sea and land

lines.text: In every place, save here in Italy.
lines.plainText: In every place save here in Italy

lines.text: I know where I will wear this dagger then;
lines.plainText: I know where I will wear this dagger then

lines.text: Cassius from bondage will deliver Cassius:
lines.plainText: Cassius from bondage will deliver Cassius

lines.text: Therein, ye gods, you make the weak most strong;
lines.plainText: Therein ye gods you make the weak most strong

lines.text: Therein, ye gods, you tyrants do defeat.
lines.plainText: Therein ye gods you tyrants do defeat

lines.text: Nor stony tower, nor walls of beaten brass,
lines.plainText: Nor stony tower nor walls of beaten brass

lines.text: Nor airless dungeon, nor strong links of iron,
lines.plainText: Nor airless dungeon nor strong links of iron

lines.text: Can be retentive to the strength of spirit;
lines.plainText: Can be retentive to the strength of spirit

lines.text: But life, being weary of these worldly bars,
lines.plainText: But life being weary of these worldly bars

lines.text: Never lacks power to dismiss itself.
lines.plainText: Never lacks power to dismiss itself

lines.text: If I know this, know all the world besides,
lines.plainText: If I know this know all the world besides

lines.text: That part of tyranny that I do bear
lines.plainText: That part of tyranny that I do bear

lines.text: I can shake off at pleasure.
lines.plainText: I can shake off at pleasure

lines.text: So can I:
lines.plainText: So can I

lines.text: So every bondman in his own hand bears
lines.plainText: So every bondman in his own hand bears

lines.text: The power to cancel his captivity.
lines.plainText: The power to cancel his captivity

lines.text: And why should Caesar be a tyrant then?
lines.plainText: And why should Caesar be a tyrant then

lines.text: Poor man! I know he would not be a wolf,
lines.plainText: Poor man I know he would not be a wolf

lines.text: But that he sees the Romans are but sheep:
lines.plainText: But that he sees the Romans are but sheep

lines.text: He were no lion, were not Romans hinds.
lines.plainText: He were no lion were not Romans hinds

lines.text: Those that with haste will make a mighty fire
lines.plainText: Those that with haste will make a mighty fire

lines.text: Begin it with weak straws. What trash is Rome,
lines.plainText: Begin it with weak straws What trash is Rome

lines.text: What rubbish, and what offal, when it serves
lines.plainText: What rubbish and what offal when it serves

lines.text: For the base matter to illuminate
lines.plainText: For the base matter to illuminate

lines.text: So vile a thing as Caesar! But, O grief,
lines.plainText: So vile a thing as Caesar But O grief

lines.text: Where hast thou led me? I, perhaps, speak this
lines.plainText: Where hast thou led me I perhaps speak this

lines.text: Before a willing bondman: then I know
lines.plainText: Before a willing bondman then I know

lines.text: My answer must be made; but I am arm'd,
lines.plainText: My answer must be made but I am arm'd

lines.text: And dangers are to me indifferent.
lines.plainText: And dangers are to me indifferent

lines.text: You speak to Casca, and to such a man
lines.plainText: You speak to Casca and to such a man

lines.text: That is no fleering tell-tale. Hold, my hand:
lines.plainText: That is no fleering telltale Hold my hand

lines.text: Be factious for redress of all these griefs,
lines.plainText: Be factious for redress of all these griefs

lines.text: And I will set this foot of mine as far
lines.plainText: And I will set this foot of mine as far

lines.text: As who goes farthest.
lines.plainText: As who goes farthest

lines.text: There's a bargain made.
lines.plainText: There's a bargain made

lines.text: Now know you, Casca, I have mov'd already
lines.plainText: Now know you Casca I have mov'd already

lines.text: Some certain of the noblest-minded Romans
lines.plainText: Some certain of the noblestminded Romans

lines.text: To undergo with me an enterprise
lines.plainText: To undergo with me an enterprise

lines.text: Of honourable-dangerous consequence;
lines.plainText: Of honourabledangerous consequence

lines.text: And I do know by this, they stay for me
lines.plainText: And I do know by this they stay for me

lines.text: In Pompey's Porch: for now, this fearful night,
lines.plainText: In Pompey's Porch for now this fearful night

lines.text: There is no stir or walking in the streets;
lines.plainText: There is no stir or walking in the streets

lines.text: And the complexion of the element
lines.plainText: And the complexion of the element

lines.text: In favour's like the work we have in hand,
lines.plainText: In favour's like the work we have in hand

lines.text: Most bloody, fiery, and most terrible.
lines.plainText: Most bloody fiery and most terrible

lines.text: Stand close awhile, for here comes one in haste.
lines.plainText: Stand close awhile for here comes one in haste

lines.text: 'Tis Cinna; I do know him by his gait;
lines.plainText: 'Tis Cinna I do know him by his gait

lines.text: He is a friend. Cinna, where haste you so?
lines.plainText: He is a friend Cinna where haste you so

lines.text: To find out you. Who's that? Metellus Cimber?
lines.plainText: To find out you Who's that Metellus Cimber

lines.text: No, it is Casca, one incorporate
lines.plainText: No it is Casca one incorporate

lines.text: To our attempts. Am I not stay'd for, Cinna?
lines.plainText: To our attempts Am I not stay'd for Cinna

lines.text: I am glad on't. What a fearful night is this!
lines.plainText: I am glad on't What a fearful night is this

lines.text: There's two or three of us have seen strange sights.
lines.plainText: There's two or three of us have seen strange sights

lines.text: Am I not stay'd for? tell me.
lines.plainText: Am I not stay'd for tell me

lines.text: Yes, you are. O Cassius, if you could
lines.plainText: Yes you are O Cassius if you could

lines.text: But win the noble Brutus to our party—
lines.plainText: But win the noble Brutus to our party

lines.text: Be you content. Good Cinna, take this paper,
lines.plainText: Be you content Good Cinna take this paper

lines.text: And look you lay it in the praetor's chair,
lines.plainText: And look you lay it in the praetor's chair

lines.text: Where Brutus may but find it; and throw this
lines.plainText: Where Brutus may but find it and throw this

lines.text: In at his window; set this up with wax
lines.plainText: In at his window set this up with wax

lines.text: Upon old Brutus' statue: all this done,
lines.plainText: Upon old Brutus' statue all this done

lines.text: Repair to Pompey's Porch, where you shall find us.
lines.plainText: Repair to Pompey's Porch where you shall find us

lines.text: Is Decius Brutus and Trebonius there?
lines.plainText: Is Decius Brutus and Trebonius there

lines.text: All but Metellus Cimber, and he's gone
lines.plainText: All but Metellus Cimber and he's gone

lines.text: To seek you at your house. Well, I will hie,
lines.plainText: To seek you at your house Well I will hie

lines.text: And so bestow these papers as you bade me.
lines.plainText: And so bestow these papers as you bade me

lines.text: That done, repair to Pompey's theatre.
lines.plainText: That done repair to Pompey's theatre

lines.text: O, he sits high in all the people's hearts!
lines.plainText: O he sits high in all the people's hearts

lines.text: And that which would appear offence in us,
lines.plainText: And that which would appear offence in us

lines.text: His countenance, like richest alchemy,
lines.plainText: His countenance like richest alchemy

lines.text: Will change to virtue and to worthiness.
lines.plainText: Will change to virtue and to worthiness

lines.text: Him, and his worth, and our great need of him,
lines.plainText: Him and his worth and our great need of him

lines.text: You have right well conceited. Let us go,
lines.plainText: You have right well conceited Let us go

lines.text: For it is after midnight; and ere day,
lines.plainText: For it is after midnight and ere day

lines.text: We will awake him, and be sure of him.
lines.plainText: We will awake him and be sure of him
